questions.question: Yash travels 204 km at 68 km/hr, the next 424 km at 53 km/hr and the next 366 km at 61 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey? (Corrected to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

Total Distance = 204 + 424 + 366 = 994 km

Total Time = (204 ÷ 68) + (424 ÷ 53) + (366 ÷ 61) = 3 + 8 + 6 = 17 hours

Average Speed = 994 ÷ 17 ≈ 58.47 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 58.47 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bac1af4b8fdb7e040a62d0a4ac5c2b7bd4f47168d297a3d24c8a7bd4f58be864.png] 

**Given:**

D₁ = 204 km, S₁ = 68 km/hr

D₂ = 424 km, S₂ = 53 km/hr

D₃ = 366 km, S₃ = 61 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = (D₁ + D₂ + D₃) ÷ (T₁ + T₂ + T₃)

**Calculations:**

⇒ T₁ = 204 ÷ 68 = 3 hours

⇒ T₂ = 424 ÷ 53 = 8 hours

⇒ T₃ = 366 ÷ 61 = 6 hours

⇒ Total Time = 3 + 8 + 6 = 17 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 204 + 424 + 366 = 994 km

⇒ Average Speed = 994 ÷ 17

⇒ Average Speed = 58.4705... ≈ 58.47 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 58.47 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, the average speed is (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

Relative speed is the sum of speeds if moving in opposite directions (S₁ + S₂) and the difference if moving in the same direction (S₁ − S₂).

Conversion Factor

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Train A running at a speed of 99 km/hr takes 46 seconds to completely cross train B running at 72 km/hr in the opposite direction. The length of train B is 1.5 times the length of train A. Train B crosses a bridge completely in 82 seconds. The length of the bridge (in m) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** = 99 + 72 = 171 km/hr = 171 × (5/18) = 47.5 m/s.

Total Length (A + B) = 47.5 × 46 = 2185 m.

Length Ratio A : B = 1 : 1.5 = 2 : 3 ⇒ 5 units = 2185 m ⇒ 1 unit = 437 m.

Length of **Train B** = 3 × 437 = 1311 m.

Speed of B = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s. Bridge Crossing: 20 × 82 = 1640 m.

**Bridge Length** = 1640 − 1311 = 329 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 329 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cbf7f478e2406e50ae9a27e6499b01873833e83b2897e9137733cb0bdaa2e46.png] 

**Given:** Speed A = 99 km/hr, Speed B = 72 km/hr, Time = 46 s, Length B = 1.5 × Length A.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time; Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂.

⇒ Relative Speed = (99 + 72) × (5/18) = 171 × (5/18) = 47.5 m/s.

⇒ Total Distance = LA + LB = 47.5 × 46 = 2185 m.

⇒ Since LB = 1.5 LA, then LA + 1.5 LA = 2185 ⇒ 2.5 LA = 2185.

⇒ LA = 2185 ÷ 2.5 = 874 m.

⇒ LB = 1.5 × 874 = 1311 m.

⇒ Speed of Train B in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.

⇒ Distance covered in 82 s = Speed B × Time = 20 × 82 = 1640 m.

⇒ Bridge Length = Total Distance − LB = 1640 − 1311 = 329 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 329 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When moving in the **opposite direction**, speeds are added (S₁ + S₂). In the **same direction**, speeds are subtracted (|S₁ − S₂|).

Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train or a bridge, the **total distance** covered is the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Ravi travels from City A to City B. If Ravi drives his car at (2)/(7) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 30 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Ravi would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio = 2 : 7 (New : Normal)

Since distance is constant, Time ratio = 7 : 2 (New : Normal)

Difference in time units = 7 − 2 = 5 units

5 units = 30 minutes ⇒ 1 unit = 6 minutes

Normal time = 2 units = 2 × 6 = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** New speed = 2/7 of Normal speed, Time delay = 30 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time; If Speed ratio is a : b, then Time ratio is b : a for a fixed distance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3de71664811bdba431341d17b4c3eb6490dcff57235320252f540bffb3f299f4.png] 

⇒ Let normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ New speed = (2/7)S

⇒ New time = T + 30

⇒ S × T = (2/7)S × (T + 30)

⇒ T = (2/7) × (T + 30)

⇒ 7T = 2T + 60

⇒ 5T = 60

⇒ T = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the distance traveled is constant, the speed is inversely proportional to the time taken (S ∝ 1/T).

Average Speed

If a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by 2xy/(x + y).

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. For opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: A boat takes 75 minutes to go 62.3 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 3 : 2. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 67.6 km upstream and 35.8 km downstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Upstream Speed** (u) = 62.3 ÷ (75/60) = 49.84 kmph.

Ratio of **Boat Speed** (v) to **Stream Speed** (s) = 3 : 2 ⇒ Upstream ratio (v − s) = 1 unit.

1 unit = 49.84 kmph ⇒ **Downstream Speed** (v + s) = 5 units = 249.2 kmph.

**Total Time** = (67.6 ÷ 49.84) + (35.8 ÷ 249.2) ≈ 1.356 + 0.144 = 1.5 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Upstream distance = 62.3 km, Time = 75 mins = 1.25 hours. Ratio of **Boat** to **Stream** speed = 3x : 2x.

**Formula:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Upstream speed (u) = v − s; Downstream speed (d) = v + s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b0053ed72d5800008c4b087033be3e5cdd93d4a20e76bbb5a78fc44d07a651f.png] 

⇒ **Upstream speed** (u) = 62.3 ÷ 1.25 = 49.84 kmph.

⇒ Let **Still water speed** (v) = 3x and **Stream speed** (s) = 2x.

⇒ Upstream speed (u) = 3x − 2x = x ⇒ x = 49.84 kmph.

⇒ **Downstream speed** (d) = 3x + 2x = 5x = 5 × 49.84 = 249.2 kmph.

⇒ Time for 67.6 km upstream = 67.6 ÷ 49.84 ≈ 1.3563 hours.

⇒ Time for 35.8 km downstream = 35.8 ÷ 249.2 ≈ 0.1437 hours.

⇒ **Total Time** = 1.3563 + 0.1437 = 1.5 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Water

Upstream Speed (u) = v − s and Downstream Speed (d) = v + s, where v is **boat speed** in still water and s is **stream speed**.

Still Water and Stream Speed Formulas

Boat speed (v) = (d + u) ÷ 2 and Stream speed (s) = (d − u) ÷ 2.

Average Speed of Boat

If the boat covers the same distance upstream and downstream, Average Speed = (u × d) ÷ v = (v² − s²) ÷ v.</p

questions.question: A 120 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 9 km/hr (in same direction) in 18 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will this train take to completely cross another 230 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 27 km/hr?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Train − Man) = 120 ÷ 18 × 18/5 = 24 km/hr

**Speed of Train** (V₁) = 24 + 9 = 33 km/hr

**Relative Speed** (Opposite Direction) = 33 + 27 = 60 km/hr

**Total Distance** = 120 + 230 = 350 m

**Time Required** = 350 ÷ (60 × 5/18) = 350 × 3 ÷ 50 = 21 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 21 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e8cc129546adeeefec513c5542c0dea5e5ec52bf99d8ff0c297a26afa4dfcb1.png] 

**Given:** Length of **Train 1** = 120 m, Speed of **Man** = 9 km/hr, Time to cross man = 18 s, Length of **Train 2** = 230 m, Speed of **Train 2** = 27 km/hr.

**Formula:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Relative Speed (Same) = V₁ − V₂; Relative Speed (Opposite) = V₁ + V₂

⇒ Let Speed of Train 1 be V₁ km/hr.

⇒ (V₁ − 9) × 5/18 = 120/18

⇒ (V₁ − 9) × 5 = 120

⇒ V₁ − 9 = 24

⇒ **V₁** = 33 km/hr

⇒ Total Distance for crossing Train 2 = 120 + 230 = 350 m

⇒ Relative Speed in opposite direction = 33 + 27 = 60 km/hr

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s

⇒ **Time** = 350 ÷ (50/3) = (350 × 3) ÷ 50 = 7 × 3 = 21 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 21 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed Rules

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference (u − v). When they move in **opposite directions**, it is the sum (u + v).

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses a **man or pole**, distance = Length of train. When it crosses another **train or platform**, distance = Sum of both lengths.</p

questions.question: A boat takes 27 minutes to go 40.6 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 8 : 7. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 77.7 km upstream and 52.5 km downstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Speed of Boat (u)** : **Speed of Stream (v)** = 8 : 7

**Upstream Speed (u−v)** = 8 − 7 = 1 unit | **Downstream Speed (u+v)** = 8 + 7 = 15 units

Given 1 unit = 40.6 km ÷ (27/60) hours = 90.22 kmph (approx calculation not needed)

**Total Time** = (77.7 ÷ 1 unit) + (52.5 ÷ 15 units) = 77.7 + 3.5 = 81.2 units of time relative to upstream

Calculating **Actual Time**: (81.2 × 27) ÷ (40.6 × 60) = 0.9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 0.9 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05dce8ef6f9a76ecfef5217e26f0b06dc7052b22caa12f3b6205d8b6064f5121.png] 

**Given:** Upstream Distance = 40.6 km, Time = 27 min = 27/60 hours

**Formula:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Upstream Speed = u − v; Downstream Speed = u + v

⇒ **Upstream Speed** = 40.6 ÷ (27/60) = (40.6 × 60) ÷ 27 = 2436 ÷ 27 = 270.66/3 kmph

⇒ Let **Speed of Boat** = 8x and **Speed of Stream** = 7x

⇒ Upstream Speed (u − v) = 8x − 7x = x

⇒ x = 40.6 × (60/27) = 243.6 ÷ 2.7 = 90.22... kmph

⇒ Downstream Speed (u + v) = 8x + 7x = 15x

⇒ **Total Time** = (77.7 ÷ x) + (52.5 ÷ 15x)

⇒ Total Time = (77.7 ÷ x) + (3.5 ÷ x) = 81.2 ÷ x

⇒ Total Time = 81.2 ÷ [40.6 × (60/27)] = (81.2 × 27) ÷ (40.6 × 60)

⇒ Total Time = 2 × (27/60) = 54 ÷ 60 = 0.9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 0.9 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Upstream and Downstream Speed

Upstream speed = u − v and Downstream speed = u + v, where u is speed in still water and v is stream speed.

Speed in Still Water from U & D

Speed of boat in still water (u) = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream from U & D

Speed of stream (v) = (Downstream − Upstream) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: A man covers distances of 819 km, 1476 km, and 1053 km at the speeds of 63 km/hr, x km/hr, and 81 km/hr, respectively. If his average speed for the whole journey is 54 km/hr, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 819 + 1476 + 1053 = 3348 km

Total time = Total distance ÷ Average speed = 3348 ÷ 54 = 62 hours

Time for 1st and 3rd parts = (819 ÷ 63) + (1053 ÷ 81) = 13 + 13 = 26 hours

Time for 2nd part = 62 − 26 = 36 hours

x = 1476 ÷ 36 = 41 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 41 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3685f32de9ffc1e673f679a47be518ba83b7a584fbc4da38e1d82f35d718eec4.png] 

**Given:**

Distances: D₁ = 819 km, D₂ = 1476 km, D₃ = 1053 km

Speeds: S₁ = 63 km/hr, S₂ = x km/hr, S₃ = 81 km/hr

Average Speed (Vₐvg) = 54 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 819 + 1476 + 1053 = 3348 km

⇒ Total Time (T) = 3348 ÷ 54 = 62 hours

⇒ T₁ = 819 ÷ 63 = 13 hours

⇒ T₃ = 1053 ÷ 81 = 13 hours

⇒ T₂ = T − (T₁ + T₃) = 62 − (13 + 13) = 62 − 26 = 36 hours

⇒ Speed x = D₂ ÷ T₂ = 1476 ÷ 36

⇒ x = 41 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 41 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, then Average Speed = 2uv ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

In the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In the opposite direction, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A boat travels 14 km upstream in 14 hours and 171 km downstream in 9 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?

**Downstream Speed** (v) = 171 ÷ 9 = 19 km/hr

**Still Water Speed** = (u + v) ÷ 2 = (1 + 19) ÷ 2 = 10 km/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Upstream distance = 14 km, Upstream time = 14 hours

Downstream distance = 171 km, Downstream time = 9 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed in Still Water (x) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a173b0dffb1723dcd4dd1d053e8f91771e9fffb269d9c39ed9279105b597b4bf.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream Speed (u) = 14 km ÷ 14 hr = 1 km/hr

⇒ Downstream Speed (v) = 171 km ÷ 9 hr = 19 km/hr

⇒ Speed of boat in still water (x) = (19 + 1) ÷ 2

⇒ x = 20 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 10 km/hr

Speed of Stream

The speed of the current or stream (y) is calculated as half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: y = (v − u) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Water

Downstream speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream (x + y); Upstream speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream (x − y).

Average Speed of Boat

If a boat travels a certain distance and returns to the starting point, Average Speed = (u × v) ÷ x, where x is speed in still water.</p

questions.question: A local train without stoppages runs at an average speed of 88 km/hr, and with stoppages, at an average speed of 24 km/hr. What is the total time (in hours) taken by the local train for stoppages on a route of length 528 km?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Stoppage time per hour** = (Difference in speed ÷ Faster speed)

**Stoppage time per hour** = (88 − 24) ÷ 88 = 64 ÷ 88 = 8/11 hours

**Total travel time (with stoppages)** = Distance ÷ Speed with stoppages = 528 ÷ 24 = 22 hours

**Total stoppage time** = 22 × (8/11) = 2 × 8 = 16 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e37dd7306092924e8673475669cad5badd518e760a026ea8f85211b7c7ae4f57.png] 
**Given:**

Average speed without stoppages = 88 km/hr

Average speed with stoppages = 24 km/hr

Total distance = 528 km

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken without stoppages = Distance ÷ Speed = 528 ÷ 88

⇒ Time taken without stoppages = 6 hours

⇒ Time taken with stoppages = Distance ÷ Speed = 528 ÷ 24

⇒ Time taken with stoppages = 22 hours

⇒ Total stoppage time = Time (with stops) − Time (without stops)

⇒ Total stoppage time = 22 − 6 = 16 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Stoppage Time Calculation

The formula for stoppage time per hour is: (Sfₐₛₜ − Sₛₗₒw) ÷ Sfₐₛₜ. Multiply this by total travel time to get absolute stoppage time.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. Stoppages reduce the average speed because they increase the total time taken for the same distance.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first one walks at 12.6 km/hr. The other one walks at 27 km/hr. The train takes 12.5 and 14 seconds, respectively, to overtake them. What is the speed of the train if both the persons are walking in the same direction as the train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **same direction**, (ST − S₁) × T₁ = (ST − S₂) × T₂ = **Length of Train**.

(ST − 12.6) × 12.5 = (ST − 27) × 14

12.5ST − 157.5 = 14ST − 378

1.5ST = 220.5 ⇒ ST = 220.5 ÷ 1.5 = 147 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 147 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/427b1d5173fa18e13287ec5a4e99a42e7ea1265dd5541fb224ee8ea5033ab0f6.png] 

**Given:** Speed of **Person 1** (S₁) = 12.6 km/hr, Time 1 (T₁) = 12.5 s

**Given:** Speed of **Person 2** (S₂) = 27 km/hr, Time 2 (T₂) = 14 s

**Formula:** Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Let **Train Speed** be S km/hr.

⇒ Length L = (S − 12.6) × (5/18) × 12.5 --- (i)

⇒ Length L = (S − 27) × (5/18) × 14 --- (ii)

⇒ (S − 12.6) × 12.5 = (S − 27) × 14

⇒ 12.5S − 157.5 = 14S − 378

⇒ 14S − 12.5S = 378 − 157.5

⇒ 1.5S = 220.5

⇒ S = 220.5 ÷ 1.5 = 147 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 147 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When moving in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference (u − v). When moving in **opposite directions**, it is the sum (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Train Overtaking a Moving Object

Length of Train = (Relative Speed) × (Time taken to cross). This formula assumes the length of the person/point object is negligible.</p

questions.question: A 250 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 7 km/hr (in same direction) in 50 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will this train take to completely cross another 280 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 28 km/hr?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Step 1: Relative Speed (v₁ − 7) × 5/18 = 250 / 50 ⇒ v₁ − 7 = 18 ⇒ **Train Speed** = 25 km/hr.

Step 2: **Relative Speed** (Opposite) = 25 + 28 = 53 km/hr.

Step 3: Total Distance = 250 + 280 = 530 m.

Step 4: Time = 530 / (53 × 5/18) = 10 × 18 / 5 = 36 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 seconds.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af4432ae7f067fe26ce3861094ef673dacea5d8ff7047869a18a2995a127218e.png] 

**Given:** Length of train 1 (L₁) = 250 m, Man speed = 7 km/hr, Time to cross man = 50 s, Length of train 2 (L₂) = 280 m, Speed of train 2 (v₂) = 28 km/hr.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance / Time; Relative speed (same direction) = v₁ − v₂; Relative speed (opposite direction) = v₁ + v₂; 1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s.

⇒ Case 1 (Train crosses man): Relative Speed = L₁ / Time

⇒ (v₁ − 7) × 5/18 = 250 / 50

⇒ (v₁ − 7) × 5/18 = 5

⇒ v₁ − 7 = 18 ⇒ v₁ = 25 km/hr

⇒ Case 2 (Train crosses train 2): Time = (L₁ + L₂) / (v₁ + v₂)

⇒ Time = (250 + 280) / [(25 + 28) × 5/18]

⇒ Time = 530 / (53 × 5/18) = (530 × 18) / (53 × 5)

⇒ Time = 10 × 18 / 5 = 2 × 18 = 36 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 36 seconds.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is |v₁ − v₂|. When they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed is v₁ + v₂.

Crossing Distance Rule

To cross a stationary point object (man, pole, tree), the train travels its **own length**. To cross another object with length (platform, bridge, train), it travels **Sum of Lengths**.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first one walks at 12.6 km/hr. The other one walks at 30.6 km/hr. The train takes 19.8 and 25.8 seconds, respectively, to overtake them. What is the speed of the train if both the persons are walking in the same direction as the train?

In same direction, **Relative Speed** = **Train Speed** (V) − **Person Speed**.

Since **Length of Train** (L) is constant: (V − 12.6) × 19.8 = (V − 30.6) × 25.8.

3.3V − 41.58 = 4.3V − 131.58 ⇒ V = 90 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3b0ba8d1265badd00933b77d2e1c4eba13c5ad5158c4d81b8b48f83f66cc4cc.png] 

**Given:** Speed of P1 = 12.6 km/hr, Speed of P2 = 30.6 km/hr, Time1 = 19.8 s, Time2 = 25.8 s.

**Formula:** Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Let Train Speed be **V** km/hr. Length of train **L** is same in both cases.

⇒ L = (V − 12.6) × (5/18) × 19.8 --- (1)

⇒ L = (V − 30.6) × (5/18) × 25.8 --- (2)

⇒ (V − 12.6) × 19.8 = (V − 30.6) × 25.8

⇒ 19.8V − 249.48 = 25.8V − 789.48

⇒ 6V = 540

⇒ V = 90 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Train Overtaking a Person

The distance covered by the train to cross/overtake a person is equal to the **length of the train** itself.</p

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 7 km/hr and the speed of the stream is 5 km/hr. A man rows to a place at a distance of 52.8 km and comes back to the starting point. Find the total time (in hours) taken by him.

**Downstream Speed** = 7 + 5 = 12 km/hr

**Upstream Speed** = 7 − 5 = 2 km/hr

**Total Time** = (52.8 ÷ 12) + (52.8 ÷ 2) = 4.4 + 26.4 = 30.8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 30.8 hours.**

Speed of boat in still water (u) = 7 km/hr

Speed of stream (v) = 5 km/hr

Upstream Speed (Sᵤ) = u − v

Total Time = Tdₒwₙ + Tᵤₚ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sd = 7 + 5 = 12 km/hr

⇒ Sᵤ = 7 − 5 = 2 km/hr

⇒ Time taken downstream = 52.8 ÷ 12 = 4.4 hours

⇒ Time taken upstream = 52.8 ÷ 2 = 26.4 hours

⇒ Total time = 4.4 + 26.4 = 30.8 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed of Boat

The average speed for a round trip is calculated as (Sd × Sᵤ) / u, where u is speed in still water.

Finding u and v from speeds

Speed in still water (u) = (Sd + Sᵤ) ÷ 2 and Speed of stream (v) = (Sd − Sᵤ) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed Concept

In downstream, the stream helps the boat (addition), while in upstream, the stream opposes the boat (subtraction).</p

questions.question: A 100 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 9 km/hr (in same direction) in 30 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will this train take to completely cross another 220 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 51 km/hr?

questions.question: A local train without stoppages runs at an average speed of 70 km/hr, and with stoppages, at an average speed of 30 km/hr. What is the total time (in hours) taken by the local train for stoppages on a route of length 630 km?
questions.solution:

Time for stoppages per hour = (Fast Speed − Slow Speed) ÷ Fast Speed

Stoppage time per hour = (70 − 30) ÷ 70 = 40/70 = 4/7 hours

Total time with stoppages = Total Distance ÷ Speed with stoppages = 630 ÷ 30 = 21 hours

Total stoppage time = 21 × (4/7) = 12 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Average speed **without stoppages** = 70 km/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a524e0cdf32f87b21bb61a71b19f69600ad962e6a8c632e16de1ee33380566c0.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual travel time (without stoppages) = Distance ÷ Speed without stoppages

⇒ Travel time = 630 ÷ 70 = 9 hours

⇒ Total time taken (with stoppages) = Distance ÷ Speed with stoppages

⇒ Total time = 630 ÷ 30 = 21 hours

⇒ Stoppage time = Total time − Actual travel time

⇒ Stoppage time = 21 − 9 = 12 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Concept

Stoppage Time Formula

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, it is S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: A man covers distances of 1980 km, 1306 km, and 540 km at the speed of 12 km/hr, x km/hr, and 36 km/hr, respectively. If his average speed for the whole journey is 14 km/hr, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Distance** = 1980 + 1306 + 540 = 3826 km

**Total Time** = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed = 3826 ÷ 14 = 273.285... hours

**Individual Times**: T₁ = 1980 ÷ 12 = 165 hours, T₃ = 540 ÷ 36 = 15 hours

**Time for middle part** = 273.285 − (165 + 15) = 93.285... hours

**Speed x** = 1306 ÷ 93.285... = 14 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 14 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e34b91395765bc6d899f90fb18709f9a482af5d75c29d51812d1d8b6547fa83e.png] 

**Given:** D₁ = 1980, S₁ = 12; D₂ = 1306, S₂ = x; D₃ = 540, S₃ = 36; Avg S = 14

**Formula Used:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Total Distance = 1980 + 1306 + 540 = 3826 km

⇒ Total Time = (1980 ÷ 12) + (1306 ÷ x) + (540 ÷ 36)

⇒ Total Time = 165 + (1306 ÷ x) + 15 = 180 + (1306 ÷ x)

⇒ 14 = 3826 ÷ [180 + (1306 ÷ x)]

⇒ 180 + (1306 ÷ x) = 3826 ÷ 14

⇒ 180 + (1306 ÷ x) = 273.2857...

⇒ 1306 ÷ x = 273.2857 − 180 = 93.2857

⇒ x = 1306 ÷ 93.2857 = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

When distances and speeds vary, Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time). Never average the speeds directly.

Special Case: Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, Average Speed = (2 × u × v) ÷ (u + v).

Conversion Factor

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

Average Speed with Equal Distances

Conversion between km/hr and m/s

questions.question: A train P going at the speed of 58 km/hr completely passes train Q of length 238 m, going in the same direction on parallel tracks, at 27 km/hr, in 7.5 minutes. How much time (in seconds) will P take to cross completely train R of length 123 m, going at 38 km/hr in the opposite direction?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Same direction) = 58 − 27 = 31 km/hr.

**Total Distance** (P + Q) = Speed × Time = (31 × 5/18) × (7.5 × 60) = (155/18) × 450 = 3875 m.

**Length of P** = 3875 − 238 = 3637 m.

**Relative Speed** (Opposite direction with R) = 58 + 38 = 96 km/hr = 96 × 5/18 = 80/3 m/s.

**Time to cross R** = (Length of P + Length of R) ÷ Relative Speed = (3637 + 123) ÷ (80/3) = 3760 × 3/80 = 47 × 3 = 141 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 141 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Total Distance = LP + 238 = (31 × 5/18) × (7.5 × 60)

⇒ LP + 238 = (155/18) × 450 ⇒ LP + 238 = 3875

⇒ LP = 3875 − 238 = 3637 m.

⇒ Relative Speed (P and R) = 58 + 38 = 96 km/hr = 96 × 5/18 = 80/3 m/s.

⇒ Time to cross R = (LP + LR) ÷ Rel. Speed = (3637 + 123) ÷ (80/3)

⇒ Time = 3760 × 3 / 80 = 47 × 3 = 141 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 141 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = V₁ − V₂. When they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed = V₁ + V₂.

Conversion Factor

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Objects

When a train crosses another train or platform, the total distance covered is the **sum of their lengths** (L₁ + L₂).</p

questions.question: Chetan travels from City A to City B. If Chetan drives his car at 2/3 of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 46 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Chetan would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is **constant**, **speed** is inversely proportional to **time**.

Ratio of **Speed** = 3 : 2 → Ratio of **Time** = 2 : 3

Difference in time units = 3 − 2 = 1 unit

Given, 1 unit = 46 minutes

Normal time = 2 units = 2 × 46 = 92 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 92 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2a02f9417088cc2238f951730fc608a5d757ad451e900d06181c39be1302991.png] 

**Given:** Reduced speed = 2/3 of normal speed. Delay = 46 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Let **Normal Speed** = S and **Normal Time** = T.

⇒ Distance = S × T

⇒ New Speed = (2/3)S and New Time = T + 46

⇒ Distance = (2/3)S × (T + 46)

⇒ S × T = (2/3)S × (T + 46)

⇒ T = 2/3 (T + 46)

⇒ 3T = 2T + 92

⇒ T = 92 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 92 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

For a constant distance, speed and time are inversely proportional (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

General Formula for Late/Early Time

If a person travels at a/b of their usual speed, the usual time taken is [Late time × a / (b − a)].

Average Speed

When distances are equal, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂).</p

questions.question: A truck travels 80 km at the speed of 40 km/hr and the next 44 km at the speed of 9 km/hr. What is its average speed (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

Total Distance = 80 + 44 = 124 km

Total Time = (80 ÷ 40) + (44 ÷ 9) = 2 + 4.888 = 6.888 hours

Average Speed = 124 ÷ (62/9) = 124 × (9/62) = 2 × 9 = 18 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Distance 1** (d₁) = 80 km, **Speed 1** (s₁) = 40 km/hr

**Distance 2** (d₂) = 44 km, **Speed 2** (s₂) = 9 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) ÷ (t₁ + t₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bfd1699f626638dfdf7248381be4c452862a752f9023e7d9a6b343ce65845e4.png] 

⇒ Time taken for first part (t₁) = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken for second part (t₂) = 44 ÷ 9 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 80 + 44 = 124 km

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 44/9 = (18 + 44) ÷ 9 = 62/9 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 124 ÷ (62/9)

⇒ Average Speed = 124 × 9 ÷ 62 = 2 × 9 = 18 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds u and v, the average speed is 2uv ÷ (u + v).

General Average Speed Formula

Average speed is always the total distance divided by the total time taken, regardless of speed variations.

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is s₁ − s₂. In opposite directions, it is s₁ + s₂.</p

questions.question: A boat takes 76 minutes to go 32.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 9 : 8. How much approximate total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 44.9 km upstream and 57.8 km downstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Speed of Boat (u)** : **Speed of Stream (v)** = 9 : 8.

**Upstream speed (u−v)** = 9x − 8x = 1x; **Downstream speed (u+v)** = 9x + 8x = 17x.

Current Upstream speed = 32.2 km ÷ (76/60) h = 25.42 kmph ⇒ x ≈ 25.42.

Total time = (44.9 ÷ x) + (57.8 ÷ 17x) = (44.9 ÷ 25.42) + (57.8 ÷ 432.14) ≈ 1.76 + 0.13 = 1.89 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.9 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd836bdb0a858fa497fd6f7e90e8fe0a80b26c8bd012a411f509bb5c152187e4.png] 

**Given:** Upstream Distance = 32.2 km, Time = 76 min, Ratio u:v = 9:8.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Upstream = u − v; Downstream = u + v.

⇒ Upstream speed (sᵤ) = 32.2 ÷ (76/60) = 32.2 × 15 / 19 = 25.421 kmph.

⇒ Let u = 9x and v = 8x. Upstream speed = 9x − 8x = x.

⇒ ∴ x = 25.421 kmph.

⇒ Downstream speed (sd) = 9x + 8x = 17x = 17 × 25.421 = 432.157 kmph.

⇒ Time for 44.9 km Upstream = 44.9 ÷ 25.421 ≈ 1.766 hours.

⇒ Time for 57.8 km Downstream = 57.8 ÷ 432.157 ≈ 0.133 hours.

⇒ Total Time = 1.766 + 0.133 = 1.899 hours ≈ 1.9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.9 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Upstream and Downstream Speeds

If **u** is boat speed in still water and **v** is stream speed, then Upstream Speed = u − v and Downstream Speed = u + v.

Average Speed of Boat

For the same distance D, Average Speed = (Upstream × Downstream) ÷ Still Water Speed.

Speed Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.</p

questions.question: Namita travels a certain distance at a speed of 88 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 16 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 33 km/hr, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the first distance is **88 km**. Then the second distance is **176 km** (double). Return distance is **88 + 176 = 264 km**.

Total Distance = 88 + 176 + 264 = **528 km**.

Total Time = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed = 528 ÷ 33 = **16 hours**.

Time for first two parts = (88 ÷ 88) + (176 ÷ 16) = 1 + 11 = **12 hours**.

Return speed = Return Distance ÷ Remaining Time = 264 ÷ (16 − 12) = 264 ÷ 4 = **66 km/hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 66 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a0338fe33cd9057c707bca99f8e3d7d1c30408158cc2296b264f185bf55eeee.png] 

**Given:** First speed = 88 km/hr, Second speed = 16 km/hr, Average speed = 33 km/hr.

**Formula:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Let distances be d, 2d, and 3d (return).

⇒ Total Distance = d + 2d + 3d = 6d

⇒ Total Time = (d/88) + (2d/16) + (3d/v) = (d/88) + (d/8) + (3d/v)

⇒ Average Speed = 6d ÷ [(d/88) + (11d/88) + (3d/v)] = 33

⇒ 6 ÷ [(12/88) + (3/v)] = 33

⇒ 6/33 = (3/22) + (3/v)

⇒ 2/11 = 3/22 + 3/v

⇒ 4/22 − 3/22 = 3/v

⇒ 1/22 = 3/v

⇒ v = 22 × 3 = 66 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 66 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If two equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = 2ab/(a+b). For three equal distances, Average Speed = 3abc/(ab+bc+ca).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is |v₁ − v₂|. In opposite directions, it is (v₁ + v₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A train P going at the speed of 78 km/hr completely passes train Q of length 120 m, going in the same direction on parallel tracks, at 62 km/hr, in 4.5 minutes. How much time (in seconds) will P take to cross completely train R of length 245 m, going at 81 km/hr in the opposite direction?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative speed** (P and Q) = 78 − 62 = 16 kmph = 16 × (5/18) m/s.

**Total distance** (LP + 120) = Speed × Time = (16 × 5/18) × (4.5 × 60) = 1200 m.

**Length of P** = 1200 − 120 = 1080 m.

**Crossing R**: Speed = 78 + 81 = 159 kmph; Distance = 1080 + 245 = 1325 m.

**Time** = 1325 ÷ (159 × 5/18) = (1325 × 18) ÷ (159 × 5) = 30 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 seconds.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b15b0bcefb5344663c14e7b10e38878cd3c49f4950b8d0435be74204e0bcb585.png] 

**Given:** SpeedP = 78 km/hr, SpeedQ = 62 km/hr, LengthQ = 120 m, TimePQ = 4.5 min. SpeedR = 81 km/hr, LengthR = 245 m.

**Formula:** Relative Speed (Same) = S₁ − S₂ | Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂ | Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Relative speed with Q = 78 − 62 = 16 km/hr = 16 × (5/18) = 40/9 m/s.

⇒ Time = 4.5 × 60 = 270 seconds.

⇒ Total Distance = LP + LQ = (40/9) × 270 = 1200 m.

⇒ LP = 1200 − 120 = 1080 m.

⇒ Relative speed with R = 78 + 81 = 159 km/hr = 159 × (5/18) m/s.

⇒ Total Distance to cross R = 1080 + 245 = 1325 m.

⇒ Required Time = 1325 ÷ (159 × 5 / 18) = (1325 × 18) ÷ 795 = 30 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 seconds.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, subtract their speeds (u − v). When they move in **opposite directions**, add their speeds (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train or a platform, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum of their lengths** (L₁ + L₂).</p

questions.question: Rishika travels a certain distance at a speed of 52 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 39 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 56 km/h, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial distance be **156 km** (LCM of 52 and 39). Total distance for outward journey = 156 + 2 × 156 = 468 km.

Outward time = (156 ÷ 52) + (312 ÷ 39) = 3 + 8 = **11 hours**.

Total journey distance (out + return) = 468 × 2 = **936 km**. Total time = 936 ÷ 56 = **117/7 hours**.

Return time = 117/7 − 11 = (117 − 77)/7 = **40/7 hours**.

Return Speed = 468 ÷ (40/7) = (468 × 7) ÷ 40 = 3276 ÷ 40 = **81.9 km/hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 81.9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9306f383fe0a30e5e9ef0c48ed871b2e6b2bc4354a0a68be9a8f41bd088ca4e3.png] 

**Given:** Speed 1 = 52 km/h, Distance 1 = D; Speed 2 = 39 km/h, Distance 2 = 2D; Average Speed = 56 km/h.

**Formula:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Total Distance = D + 2D + 3D (Return) = 6D

⇒ Total Time = (D/52) + (2D/39) + (3D/v)

⇒ 56 = 6D / [(D/52) + (2D/39) + (3D/v)]

⇒ 56 = 6 / [(3/156) + (8/156) + (3/v)]

⇒ 56 = 6 / [11/156 + 3/v]

⇒ 11/156 + 3/v = 6/56 = 3/28

⇒ 3/v = 3/28 − 11/156 = (3 × 39 − 11 × 7) / 1092 = (117 − 77) / 1092

⇒ 3/v = 40 / 1092

⇒ v = (1092 × 3) / 40 = 3276 / 40 = 81.9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 81.9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, Average Speed = 2uv / (u + v). For three equal distances, it is 3uvw / (uv + vw + wu).

Weighted Average Speed

If distances d₁, d₂,... are covered at speeds v₁, v₂,..., Average Speed = (Σdᵢ) / (Σdᵢ/vᵢ).

Time & Distance Relation

Distance = Speed × Time. If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (v₁/v₂ = t₂/t₁).</p

questions.question: A boat travels 176 km upstream in 16 hours and 85 km downstream in 5 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Upstream speed (U)** = 176 ÷ 16 = 11 km/hr

**Downstream speed (D)** = 85 ÷ 5 = 17 km/hr

**Speed in still water** = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (17 + 11) ÷ 2 = 14 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 14 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6a5f1d482740f940291229e99cc96270db2db65145cc22ea74f21aa131813b7.png] 

**Given:**

**Upstream Distance** = 176 km, **Upstream Time** = 16 hours

**Downstream Distance** = 85 km, **Downstream Time** = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed of boat in still water (x) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = 176 ÷ 16 = 11 km/hr

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = 85 ÷ 5 = 17 km/hr

⇒ x = (17 + 11) ÷ 2

⇒ x = 28 ÷ 2 = 14 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 14 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Current

The speed of the stream or current (y) is calculated as (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Water

Downstream speed = x + y and Upstream speed = x − y, where x is boat speed and y is stream speed.

Average Speed

If a boat travels to a point and returns, Average Speed = (D × U) ÷ x, where x is boat speed in still water.</p

questions.question: Amita travels a certain distance at a speed of 84 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 28 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 24 km/hr, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume first distance is 84 km. Then second distance is 168 km. Total forward distance = 252 km.

Forward time = (84 ÷ 84) + (168 ÷ 28) = 1 + 6 = 7 hours.

Total journey distance = 252 + 252 = 504 km.

Total time = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed = 504 ÷ 24 = 21 hours.

Return time = 21 − 7 = 14 hours. Return speed = 252 ÷ 14 = 18 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speed 1 = 84 km/hr, Distance 1 = d; Speed 2 = 28 km/hr, Distance 2 = 2d; Average Speed = 24 km/hr.

**Formula Used:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d722c015ca39cc8af9d04591a5e3659f9b74821a0cf09c1f4add1a4be15c1aaa.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = d + 2d + 3d = 6d

⇒ Total Time = (d ÷ 84) + (2d ÷ 28) + (3d ÷ V)

⇒ 24 = 6d ÷ [(d/84) + (6d/84) + (3d/V)]

⇒ 24 = 6d ÷ [(7d/84) + (3d/V)]

⇒ 24 = 6 ÷ [(1/12) + (3/V)]

⇒ (1/12) + (3/V) = 6/24 = 1/4

⇒ 3/V = (1/4) − (1/12) = 2/12 = 1/6

⇒ V = 18 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

For unequal distances, Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + ... + dₙ) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + ... + tₙ).

Special Case: Equal Distances

If a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Time and Distance Relation

Speed is inversely proportional to time when distance is constant: S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁.</p

questions.question: A train is 591 m and it crosses a platform in 1.7 minutes running at the speed of 36 km/hr. Find the difference between the length of the train and the platform.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Speed** to m/s: 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s.

Convert **Time** to seconds: 1.7 × 60 = 102 seconds.

Total Distance (Train + Platform) = 10 × 102 = 1020 m.

Platform Length = 1020 − 591 = 429 m.

Difference = 591 − 429 = 162 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 162 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68b3a4eeeeab2e4b55e6eadf58796ebb0241953ff4dff23991506e33f36dea73.png] 

**Given:**

Length of **Train** (Lₜ) = 591 m

**Speed** (S) = 36 km/hr = 36 × (5/18) m/s = 10 m/s

**Time** (T) = 1.7 minutes = 1.7 × 60 s = 102 s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = Lₜ + Lₚ

⇒ Total Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ 591 + Lₚ = 10 × 102

⇒ 591 + Lₚ = 1020

⇒ Lₚ = 1020 − 591 = 429 m

⇒ Required Difference = |Lₜ − Lₚ|

⇒ Difference = 591 − 429 = 162 m

**∴ The correct answer is 162 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Objects

When a train crosses a **stationary object** with length (like a platform or bridge), total distance = length of train + length of object.

Speed, Distance, Time Relation

Distance = Speed × Time. Ensure all units are in the same system (m, m/s, seconds) before calculation.</p
